name: Postgenderism
summary: Postgenderism, formulated by George Dvorsky and James Hughes in 2008, holds that gender is an arbitrary and unnecessary limitation on human potential. It expects neurotechnology, biotechnology and assisted reproduction to end involuntary biological and psychological gendering. It does not call for universal androgyny; masculine and feminine traits would become a matter of choice.
scope: The transhumanist postgenderism of Dvorsky and Hughes (2008) as set out in their abstract and Dvorsky's reply, with Biswas's scholarly account. Haraway's cyborg feminism, queer theory and wider posthumanism (Mellamphy) are context, not answers. Fiction's worldbuilding is not taken as programme. The full monograph was not accessible.
